newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies bid to delay Florida tobacco trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies bid to delay Florida tobacco trial.

text.p: A Florida judge on Thursday denied a tobacco industry motion to delay a landmark, $5 billion secondhand smoke trial, a court spokesman said.

Judge Robert Kaye, presiding over a class-action lawsuit filed by a group of U.S. flight attendants, turned away a bid by B.A.T Industries Plc's Brown and Williamson Tobacco Corp to stay the trial because of the proposed global tobacco settlement, court spokesman Mort Lucoff said.

The June 20 settlement between tobacco companies and state attorneys general would require tobacco companies to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years, cut back advertising and make health-care concessions. But it requires the approval of U.S. lawmakers and may take months to enact.

The motion was the latest in a series made by tobacco industry lawyers in recent weeks to delay the secondhand smoke trial. Kaye had previously said he did not expect the settlement to stop the trial.
Earlier Thursday, two of the 10 alternate jurors picked this week to hear the case were excused, leaving eight alternates in addition to the six members of the jury panel.
Kaye was expected to decide Friday whether to excuse a member of the main panel who clashed with a bailiff over conditions in the jury room.
Testimony in the case, known as Norma Broin et al. vs Philip Morris Cos Inc et al, is expected to take two months or more. Jury selection began on June 2.
Opening arguments are expected to begin on July 14.
The lawsuit claims thousands of flight attendants were sickened by breathing cigarette smoke on U.S. passenger jets.
